title: Trading basics: what trading really is
summary: Start from zero. Learn what a market is, why prices move, and how trading differs from investing and from gambling, with honest expectations from day one.
outcomes: Explain in your own words what a market and a trade are
Describe why prices go up and down
Tell the difference between trading, investing and gambling
Set realistic expectations for your first months of learning
lessons: Buyers, sellers and why prices move
What a beginner should (and should not) expect
Key words you will hear every day
checklist: I can explain what a market is
I know why prices move
I understand that losses are a normal part of trading
I have joined the Telegram community for Module 2

title: Markets and instruments
summary: Forex, stocks, crypto and commodities: what each market is, how currency pairs work, and when each market is open.
outcomes: Name the main markets and what is traded in each
Read a currency pair such as EUR/USD (base and quote)
Know the main trading sessions and why they matter
Understand what affects liquidity and volatility
lessons: Forex, stocks, crypto and commodities at a glance
Currency pairs: base, quote, majors and crosses
Trading sessions: Asia, London and New York
Liquidity and volatility in plain words
checklist: I can name four types of market
I can tell the base and quote currency in a pair
I know which session overlaps are the busiest

title: Reading a price chart
summary: Learn to read candlestick charts, choose a timeframe, and understand what open, high, low and close tell you.
outcomes: Read a candlestick (open, high, low, close)
Switch between timeframes and know when to use each
Recognise bullish, bearish and indecision candles
Set up a clean chart on a free charting platform
lessons: Common candle shapes, and why context matters more
checklist: I can point to the open, high, low and close of a candle
I have set up a chart with one higher and one lower timeframe
I know that one candle alone is not a signal

title: Brokers, accounts and order types
summary: How brokers work, what spread, leverage and margin mean, the different order types, and how to protect yourself from scams.
outcomes: Explain spread, commission, leverage and margin
Use market, limit and stop orders correctly
Check whether a broker is regulated and avoid common scams
Know the rules for online trading in your own country
lessons: What a broker does and how it earns money
Leverage and margin: why they magnify losses as well as gains
Order types: market, limit, stop and stop-loss
Regulation, legal checks and red flags of scams
checklist: I can explain leverage and why it is risky
I know how to place a stop-loss order
I have checked the trading rules for my country
I have opened a demo (practice) account, not a live one

title: Support, resistance and trends
summary: The foundation of chart analysis: find support and resistance zones, identify trends, and understand market structure.
outcomes: Draw support and resistance as zones, not exact lines
Identify uptrends, downtrends and ranges
Understand higher highs, higher lows and breaks of structure
Avoid drawing too many lines
checklist: I have marked support and resistance on three charts
I can tell whether a chart is trending or ranging
I posted one of my charts in the community for feedback

title: Indicators, used simply
summary: What indicators can and cannot do. Learn moving averages and RSI, and why fewer indicators usually means clearer decisions.
outcomes: Explain what an indicator is calculated from
Use moving averages to read trend direction
Read RSI without treating it as a buy/sell button
Keep a clean chart with one or two tools
lessons: Why more indicators is not better
checklist: I have added one moving average to my chart
I can explain what RSI measures
My chart has no more than two indicators

title: Risk management: the most important module
summary: Protect your account first. Learn the 1% rule, stop-losses, position sizing and risk/reward, with free calculators.
outcomes: Decide how much of your account to risk per trade
Place a stop-loss based on the chart, not on hope
Calculate position size with the free calculator
Understand risk/reward and break-even win rate
lessons: Why risk management comes before strategy
checklist: I have chosen a maximum risk per trade (for example 1%)
I have used the position-size calculator on three example trades
I understand that I can be wrong often and still manage risk

title: Building a simple trading plan
summary: Turn what you have learned into written rules: what you trade, when you enter, when you exit, and how you review.
outcomes: Write a one-page trading plan
Define clear entry, exit and no-trade rules
Create a pre-trade checklist
Plan a weekly review routine
lessons: Choosing markets, timeframes and trading hours
checklist: I have written my one-page trading plan
I have a pre-trade checklist
I shared my plan in the community for feedback

title: Trading psychology
summary: Fear, greed, revenge trading and overtrading. Learn to recognise emotional decisions and build habits that keep you disciplined.
outcomes: Recognise fear, greed and revenge trading in yourself
Use rules and checklists to reduce emotional decisions
Handle a losing streak calmly
Know when to step away from the screen
lessons: Why emotions are the hardest part
Fear of missing out and overtrading
checklist: I have written my personal 'stop trading for today' rule
I know my emotional warning signs
I have a daily routine that includes breaks

title: Practice, journaling and next steps
summary: Put everything together on a demo account. Keep a trading journal, review your results honestly and plan your next stage of learning.
outcomes: Run a structured demo practice period
Keep a trading journal with the free template
Review your trades and find one thing to improve
Plan your next stage of learning
lessons: How to practise on a demo account
checklist: I have logged at least 20 demo trades in my journal
I have done one weekly review
I know the one habit I want to improve next
